newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.
White sugar futures in London edged back to flat in late business after sustained light buying earlier took them into positive territory, traders said.
The spot March contract saw a mixture of trade and commission house buying, mainly outright, which pushed values up to $305.10. At the close March was even at $303.90 and May down $0.20 at $304.60.

Raw sugar futures in New York were near day's highs, buoyed by speculative short covering ahead of the holiday, dealers said. The spot month March contract closed up 0.06 at 10.75 cents/lb while May was up 0.04 at 10.79 cents. The outer months settled 0.03 firmer. Traders expected activities to thin on Wednesday ahead of Thursday's Thanksgiving holiday. The CSCE will be closed Thursday and Friday.

EUROPE - Rains in western Europe continued in the week ended November 26. Precipitation amounts were 12 to 15 mm across the UK, where the bulk of the unharvested sugar beet crops remain. The wet weather continues to stall the late harvest but declines have been minor since much of the crop has been harvested. Additional rainfall this week will continue to slow the harvest. Eastern Europe saw scattered 6 to 18 mm amounts, but harvest is essentially complete. In the former Soviet Union favorably dry weather conditions during the past month of the harvest lead to a slight improvement in crop production. However, output will still be lower than last year.

GERMANY - Sugar content in the week ended November 22 again crept up by 2 percentage points to 18.16 per cent against 16.74 per cent in the same week last year and 17.15 per cent in 1994. This more than compensated the lower tonnage of beet delivered for processing which reached 2.213 million tonnes against 2.330 million tonnes in 1995 and 2.331 million tonnes in 1994. Sugar production in the period under review reached 382,172 tonnes, raw value, against 357,754 tonnes in 1995. This brought cumulative production in 1996 up to 3.238 million tonnes against 2.959 million tonnes in 1995 and 3.051 million tonnes in 1994.

CUBA - According to ISO figures, sugar exports in July 1996 amounted 70,909 tonnes, raw value, down from last year's 144,753 tonnes. However, cumulative exports in the first ten months of 1995/96 (October/July) were considerably higher at 3.736 million tonnes against 2.727 million tonnes in the corresponding period the previous year. Total exports in 1994/95 amounted to 2.760 million tonnes against 3.191 million tonnes in 1993/94.

Major countries of destination in October/July 1995/96 were Russia with 1.825 million tonnes raws against 781,146 tonnes, China with 355,619 tonnes down from 740,920 tonnes, Morocco with 206,866 tonnes compared to 88,054 tonnes and Romania with 200,207 tonnes, up from 95,930 tonnes. New on the list of destinations for Cuban raws in 1995/96 were Lithuania with 73,277 tonnes, Turkey with 29,276 tonnes and Mexico with 14,719 tonnes.

The higher exports in 1995/96 are a reflection of the recovery which has taken place in the sugar sector of the island. Given the fact that another increase can be forecast for 1996/97 it is likely that sugar exports in the coming campaign will remain around the levels seen in 1995/96.
